hi Alejandro,
 when you define the fit statistic, you need to define it only in terms of the non-missing values.  This doesn't require modifying the unmarked frame at all.
 somewhere in the webinar (see link below) we talked about this with an example.

There is an example on p. 29 of the slides located here:
https://sites.google.com/site/unmarkedinfo/home/webinars/2012-january/slides/moduleABUN.pdf?attredirects=0&d=1
This example involves the use of pcount() also.

regards
andy

messages.subject: Re: NAs and parboot
parts:
Hi,

My single season occupancy model has 51 sites, each site was visited 5 times except 1 which was visited only 4 times. I used the code to omit NA's so that the parametric bootstrap will go forward, but when I get my output it tells me that there are 50 or more warnings:

In rbinom(M * J, 1, prob = p) : NAs produced

What is wrong with my code or my model that it would be doing this?

Thanks,
Rylee

ps. How do I get parboot to give me a confidence interval for an overall occupancy probability for all 51 of my sites?

fitstats <- function(d23)  {     #d23 is my model
  observed <- getY(occu.umf) #occu.umf is my unmarkedFrame
  expected <- fitted(d23)
  resids <- residuals(d23)
  r2<- resids^2
  sse <- sum(r2, na.rm=TRUE)
  chisq <- sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected, na.rm=TRUE)
  freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2, na.rm=TRUE)
  out <- c(SSE=sse, Chisq=chisq, freemanTukey=freeTuke)
  return(out)
}

(pb <- parboot(d23, fitstats, nsim=100, report=1))
plot(pb, main="")
